transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Yeah, um… I guess what finally made me bring it up is my eating after really long days. I supervise crews, and some days on site just run me into the ground, or I’ll have a neighborhood meeting that drags on and on—people get very worked up about parking and noise, you know—and then I get home and it’s like I just… keep eating.

Like, leftover takeout, cereal, chips, whatever is around. I’ll tell myself I’m just going to have something quick, and then suddenly it’s way more than I meant to eat, to the point where I’m really uncomfortably full. It’s embarrassing to say out loud, but that’s been bothering me.
Can you tell me more about those times when you start eating—do you feel like you can stop at any point, or does it feel like you lose control once you start?

Yeah… it feels like I lose control. Like once I start on those nights, I kind of go on autopilot. I’ll be standing there thinking, “You need to stop, you’ve got an early crew start tomorrow,” and then I’m still opening the cabinet or going back to the kitchen for more.

It’s weird because I can be really organized at work—like, I’m the one making sure everyone’s where they’re supposed to be, materials are lined up, safety stuff is handled—and then at home with food it’s like that part of my brain just… shuts off for a while.
When you find yourself eating like this, do you feel like you’re eating much more quickly than normal, or continuing until you feel very uncomfortable?

Yeah, I mean… the main thing I notice is I keep going way past what I intended. Like after a long day on site, or after one of those neighborhood meetings where everyone’s arguing about parking or the construction schedule, I get home and it’s just whatever’s there—leftover takeout, cereal, chips.

And then I’ll realize I’ve eaten a lot more than I meant to, like… not just a snack, but enough that I’m really uncomfortable afterward. It’s kind of like I don’t register it until I’m already too full.
Do you feel upset, ashamed, or guilty after these episodes of eating more than you intended?

I… I don’t really know how to answer that exactly. I mean, I don’t feel great afterward, because I’m uncomfortable and kind of annoyed with myself, but “ashamed” or “guilty” feels like a big word.

Sometimes I just try to clean up the kitchen and get ready for the next day, because if I start thinking too much about it I’ll get stuck there. And mornings come early on site—if a concrete delivery is late or someone’s calling out, it’s like, okay, no time to sit around analyzing last night’s cereal situation.

So… maybe upset in the sense that I wish I hadn’t done it, but I don’t know if I’d say it’s always shame or guilt.
After these episodes of eating more than you intended, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to try to compensate or make up for it?

Um… yeah. Not all the time. I don’t use laxatives or anything like that, and the exercise thing—honestly my job is physical enough most days, though I know that’s not really what you’re asking.

But… a few times a month, after one of those nights where I eat too much, I’ll get this panic feeling. Like I’ve undone everything I do to look like I have it together—work clothes, being put-together on site, people taking me seriously—and then I’ve gone into the bathroom and made myself throw up.

I don’t like saying that out loud. It’s not something I plan, exactly. It’s more like I freak out afterward and just… do it.
How often have you made yourself vomit after these episodes of eating more than you intended?

I think… if I’m being honest, looking back over the last few months, it’s probably averaged out to about once a week.

It doesn’t feel that regular in the moment, because some weeks it might happen twice—like if work’s been a mess and I’m getting home late—and then another week maybe not at all, so I tell myself it’s not really a “thing.” But when I actually add it up in my head… yeah. About weekly, I guess.
Have you ever made yourself vomit or done anything else to try to control your weight or shape, not just after eating too much, but as part of worrying about how your body looks?

Yeah… I mean, I guess it is tied to that, not just the food itself.

It’s usually after those nights when I eat way more than I meant to, and then I start spiraling about how I’m going to look the next day—like if my clothes are going to feel tight, or if I’m not going to look pulled together. Which sounds ridiculous, because I’m on a construction site half the time and everyone’s covered in dust anyway, but I still feel like I have to look like I’m in control.

So a few times a month, I’ve gone to the bathroom and made myself throw up. It’s not like some organized plan exactly. It’s more like panic—like I’ve undone all this work to seem put-together, and I need to fix it fast.

Outside of worrying about your weight or shape, do these episodes of eating more than you intend ever cause you distress or interfere with things you need to do in your daily life, like work or time with family?

Yeah… I mean, I’m still functioning. I’m still getting to work, running the crew, doing what I’m supposed to do.

But it does mess with my evenings more than I want to admit. Like after meetings, if people are grabbing food or someone says, “Let’s go get something,” I’ve started making excuses. Or I’ll rush home because I’m worried if I’m out too long the night will kind of get away from me and I’ll end up eating more than I meant to.

It’s stupid because sometimes those are good networking things, or just normal social stuff, and I’ll be like, no, I need to get home. So… yeah, it interferes some. Not like I’m missing work, but I am planning around it.
During these episodes of eating more than you intended, would you say you feel a complete lack of control over your eating, like you can't stop or control what you're doing?

Yeah… I think that’s probably the part that scares me, honestly.

Once I start on those evenings, it kind of feels like I’m on autopilot. Like I’ll be standing there thinking, okay, stop now, you’ve got an early crew start tomorrow, you need to be up before everyone else and have your head on straight… and then somehow I’m back in the kitchen getting more.

And it’s not even always that I’m enjoying it. Sometimes I’m already annoyed with myself while I’m doing it, but I still keep going. So… yeah, it does feel like I can’t really stop in the moment.

Do these episodes of eating more than you intend usually happen after you've had a stressful or emotionally difficult day, or do they also happen when you're not feeling particularly stressed or upset?

Usually after stressful days, yeah. Like, what made me even bring this up is that after these long days on site, or sometimes after a neighborhood meeting where everyone’s got opinions and I’m trying to keep things calm, I’ll get home and just… eat way more than I meant to.

It’ll be whatever’s there—leftover takeout, cereal, chips. Not even like a proper meal, just kind of standing there picking at things, then sitting down, then getting up again. And then suddenly I’m uncomfortably full.

I mean, I guess it’s not every single stressful day, and I don’t want to make it sound like the job is the only reason. Construction is always stressful in some way—permits, weather, somebody calling out, someone’s truck blocking access, you know. But the bad nights do seem to come after those really long or emotionally draining days more than random calm ones.
